root_cause.text: The fence reference obtained from amdgpu_ib_schedule() is released via dma_fence_put() before calling dma_fence_wait(), causing a use-after-free if the put operation drops the last reference and frees the fence object prior to the wait.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves dma_fence_put(f) after dma_fence_wait(f, false), and the CVE description explicitly states: "Currently, the code drops the fence reference using dma_fence_put() before calling dma_fence_wait(). If dma_fence_put() releases the last reference, the fence may be freed before dma_fence_wait() is called."

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix use-after-free by moving dma_fence_put after dma_fence_wait to keep the fence alive during the wait.
intent_record.what: Moved dma_fence_put(f) from before dma_fence_wait(f, false) to after it, and updated the comment accordingly.
intent_record.how: Previously, the fence reference was dropped before waiting, which could lead to use-after-free. Now the reference is dropped after the wait completes, ensuring the fence object remains valid during the wait.

candidates.rationale: This statement releases the fence reference obtained from amdgpu_ib_schedule() before the wait, potentially dropping the last reference and freeing the fence object, causing use-after-free in the subsequent dma_fence_wait call.
This statement uses the fence pointer f after it may have already been freed by the preceding dma_fence_put, leading to a use-after-free vulnerability when the wait accesses the freed memory.
